title: Cab Calloway comes in from the Alabamians and Blackbirds; Irving Mills
summary: After the Alabamians failed and Cab left a show, the Missourians pay him to front them; Irving Mills takes an interest and Thomas grows close to Cab.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So Lockwood left, for some reason. And we heard that Cab... Cab had come to New York with this band from Chicago...
It had another name to it. And he came to the...and this band...
Yeah, this band broke up. So Cab went with this show. So we knew of...

I don't know whether it was Blackbirds... I think he was (?) for Blackbirds. It was one of them shows. But anyway, we knew about Cab better than we did about the band, because was a showman in his band! But the band just didn't make it in New York.
What band was that? The band in this show?
Was it Jimmy Wade...? Yeah. I think the (?) band was at the Alabam Club.
Yeah, that was the name of the band.
Yeah, Eddie Mallory. I got to know him well, too.

Right. But they didn't make it, but Cab made an impression. So we found out that he was at this show... I don't know if we got Blanche to get him or what. But anyway, they got ahold of him and talked him into coming again, just to direct it. We were paying him a hundred dollars a week to just direct the band. Because that's all
we used them leaders for, is just to direct the band. We did the playing. But he had more going than anybody else. We never had no guy with all those dances and all that shakin' head...

So Mills got involved with the band... See, Mills got involved with the band because he was interested in his publishing (?). So that's how I really got close to Cab, because when we used to go downtown to pick songs, I'd go with him, because I could read, and he wasn't that much of a musician.
